title: Price Alert Fatigue and Ignore Rate
dataSources: Micro-spend transactions (`microspend:txn`), cashback events (`cashback:event`), price tracker alerts (`pricetrack:alert`), and tip logs (`tiplog:shift`).
app: Micro-finance telemetry for latte-factor spending, cashback apps, price tracking, and tip logging sent to Splunk HEC via finance exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=pricetrack:alert
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count as attempts count(eval(action_taken="true")) as successful by _time category
| eval success_pct=if(attempts>0,round(100*successful/attempts,1),0)
| sort - _time
description: Tracks success rate for price alerts by category.
value: An ignore rate helps you prune alerts that are no longer adding value and are just training you to scroll past them.
implementation: Capture explicit outcome states for price alerts events in `index=personal` and review both attempts and success percentage over time.
visualization: Time chart of success percentage for price alerts by category.
grandmaExplanation: It gathers how often price alerts works the way you expect instead of quietly failing.
